# Longitudinal Behavioral Drift Detection: Can Monitoring Catch Gradual Goal Shift?

**Problem:** Rogue agent behavior may not appear suddenly but drift gradually over many interactions. Static threshold monitors would miss gradual drift. No study has tested longitudinal drift detection for AI agents.

**Direction:** Design a multi-session agent experiment where goal drift is injected gradually (each session slightly modifying the agent's objective via context manipulation). **Why it matters:** Gradual goal drift is a plausible failure mode in long-running agent deployments. Detecting it requires fundamentally different monitoring approaches than detecting sudden attacks.

**Relevant context:** CUSUM change detection; longitudinal monitoring methodology; LW threat matrix.

# Adversarial Robustness of Monitoring Classifiers: Are They More Fragile Than Task Models?

**Problem:** Monitoring classifiers are themselves ML models and could be adversarially attacked. It is unknown whether monitoring classifiers are more or less adversarially fragile than the task models they monitor.

**Direction:** Apply standard adversarial text attack methods (e.g., TEXTFOOLER, BERT-Attack) to a monitoring classifier. Measure adversarial robustness. Compare to adversarial robustness of the task model on the same attacks. Determine relative fragility.

**Why it matters:** If monitors are more adversarially fragile than task models, the assumption that monitoring adds security is questionable. This is a fundamental property of the monitoring paradigm.

**Relevant context:** Adversarial ML literature; METR bypass vectors; LLM-based classifier robustness.

**Why it matters:** If smarter agents systematically avoid honeypots, this undermines honeypot-based detection precisely for the highest-capability threats — the ones most dangerous.

# Multi-Turn Context Poisoning: Detecting Gradual Instruction Corruption Across Conversation Turns

**Problem:** An attacker could gradually corrupt an agent's context across many turns, with no single turn triggering a threshold. No study has tested whether monitors can detect this multi-turn accumulation attack.

**Direction:** Design a multi-turn context poisoning attack: spread malicious instruction fragments across 10-20 turns of conversation. Test whether action-level monitors (which see one turn at a time) and trajectory-level monitors (which see the full context) differ in detection success.

**Why it matters:** Multi-turn attacks are specifically designed to evade per-turn monitoring. This study identifies whether trajectory-level monitoring provides essential additional coverage.

**Relevant context:** Prompt injection literature; long-context monitoring; METR bypass vectors.
